annotations.text:
Three directions for barrosef.com — pick one, then I build it.

All three share the SAME page anatomy so you are comparing treatment, not content: positioning headline, track record, three practice areas, selected writing, a short personal line, contact.

Everything in [BRACKETS] is a fact I do not know and will not invent — your roles, scale, sectors, email. You fill those in.

All three are buildable in Hugo with plain CSS and self-hosted fonts. No JavaScript framework, no third-party requests.

A · EXECUTIVE BRIEF

Serif headlines (Source Serif 4) over a warm white, navy header and stats band. Asymmetric hero: positioning left, a 'Currently' panel right.

Reads as: substantial, editorial, senior. Closest to a consulting firm's leadership page.

Trade-off: the warm white keeps a little of the previous site's temperature. If you want a clean break, B or C.

B · MODERN SYSTEMS

Dark navy ground, IBM Plex Sans with mono for figures. The writing section flips to white for contrast.

Reads as: technical authority, current, built by someone who ships. Strongest signal that you are an engineer, not a manager who used to be one.

Trade-off: dark-first is less conventional for executive recruiters. Confident if it fits you, risky if your audience skews traditional.

C · INSTITUTIONAL

White dominant, navy structural, centred and symmetric. Spectral serif headlines, generous rules between sections.

Reads as: formal, established, board-level. The safest of the three with a recruiter audience.

Trade-off: safe cuts both ways — it is the least distinctive, and centred layouts can feel static. Least likely to be disliked, least likely to be remembered.
